summary: DIYhomie Project Handoffs (Shopping List + Home Report, namespace /api/hi/handoff/*) tested end-to-end. Backend pytest: 8/8 PASS covering (1) GET /shopping/{pid} returns 2 items with to_buy_total=$202, owned_total=$0, grand_total=$202, both items default to need_to_buy, Faucet has quantity 1 and estimate 180, (2) POST /shopping/{pid}/items/{material_rid}/purchased?purchased=true responds ok=true and re-GET shows owned_total=$180, to_buy_total=$22, grand_total=$202, the specific item flips owned=true/status=owned, (3) toggling purchased=false restores owned_total=$0 and to_buy_total=$202 (proves toggle is bidirectional, not a one-way write), (4) cross-user GET /shopping and POST /shopping/.../purchased both return 404 for a freshly-registered second user, (5) GET /report/{pid} on a non-completed project returns completed=false with all required keys (title, project_type, materials_used, tools_used, approx_cost, confirmed_savings, tasks_completed, known_limitations, share_text) and share_text contains the project title, (6) after resolving risks, marking all tasks complete and POST /orchestrator/projects/{id}/complete the same /report returns completed=true and share_text contains 'Completed', (7) cross-user GET /report returns 404. Frontend (mobile 390x844, demo login): navigating to /home-intel/orchestrator/{completed_pid} shows pd-shopping and pd-report cards alongside pd-fund/pd-back/pd-events. pd-shopping opens Shopping List with STILL TO BUY $202.00 / Owned $0.00 / Total $202.00 and two shop-item-* rows (Faucet x1 $180.00, Basin wrench $22.00). Tapping the Faucet row triggers POST purchased=true and the header updates live to STILL TO BUY $22.00 / Owned $180.00 / Total $202.00 with the item text showing line-through and 'Material · Owned'. Tapping it again toggles back. pd-report opens Home Report showing 'Completed Project' status, Summary card (Type Bathroom Remodel, Tasks Completed 9, Approx. Cost $202.00), MATERIALS USED (Faucet), TOOLS USED (Basin wrench), the homeowner-record disclaimer, and both a rep-share icon in the header and a full-width rep-share-btn 'Share report' button that fires Share.share without exceptions. Cross-user 404 isolation verified for both surfaces. No red screens, no 500s, no crashes.
critical_code_review_comments: handoff_engine.py line 78 (mark_purchased): the item lookup filters by user_id but the parent _owned(project_id, user_id) already enforced ownership, and orch_requirements sometimes may not carry user_id on legacy rows. Behaviour today is correct for freshly-created requirements but consider one canonical scoping (either project-scoped after _owned, or user-scoped) to avoid a silent 404 for older data.

handoff_engine.py line 104: approx_cost falls back to sum(cost_estimate) when there is no passport, which is exactly what the report shows for in-progress projects; but if a user has already toggled some items to 'owned' with a $0 saving applied via funding, those still count at their full cost_estimate here. This matches the current 'estimates only' contract but is worth calling out in the UI copy so users don't double-read the number as 'money still to spend'.

handoff_engine.py line 114: known_limitations queries every risk regardless of state; resolved risks are also reported as limitations on the home report. Consider filtering to state!='resolved' (or only including safety/verify holds) so the shareable report doesn't advertise issues the homeowner already cleared.
seed_data_creation: The pytest module fixture creates a fresh orchestrator project ('replace kitchen faucet') with a Faucet material ($180) and Basin wrench tool ($22) requirement for demo_home@diyhomie.com, then completes it (resolves risks, marks all tasks complete, POST /complete) to exercise the completed-report path. It also registers one throwaway TEST_handoff_*@diyhomie.com user solely to assert 404 cross-user isolation. Frontend test reused the completed project id e409128c-fbe3-424d-9e63-6e4ada8a3aa6 produced by the backend run.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Handoff testIDs on the project detail screen: pd-shopping, pd-report (both live in /app/frontend/app/home-intel/orchestrator/[id].tsx alongside pd-fund). Shopping screen (shopping/[id].tsx) exposes shop-back and shop-item-{requirement_id}; the whole row is a Pressable that flips purchased state via POST /api/hi/handoff/shopping/{pid}/items/{rid}/purchased?purchased={true|false}. Report screen (report/[id].tsx) exposes rep-back, rep-share (header icon) and rep-share-btn (full-width button); both invoke React Native Share.share with the backend-generated share_text. Login path: root -> 'I already have an account' -> two inputs -> 'Log in'. Fastest way into a project detail is to navigate directly to /home-intel/orchestrator/{project_id} after login, since the home-resume chip and Home 'Replace a kitchen faucet' pill both create/enter a new drafting project.
